title: Defense AI Reliability and Reporting Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.
summary: This act requires that all AI systems used in defense meet strict reliability standards and that their developers report performance and safety data to oversight authorities. The goal is to ensure AI employed in national security is trustworthy, transparent, and accountable.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a piece of legislation designed to stop artificial intelligence from being used to spread misinformation or otherwise manipulate voter behavior during elections. It would set out rules, reporting requirements, and enforcement powers to help keep the voting process fair and secure.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act requires developers of AI systems that can modify themselves to report their updates and performance to a central oversight body. It also establishes safety standards, audit procedures, and transparency rules to ensure that these self‑adjusting systems do not pose unforeseen risks to users or society.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act would halt the construction of new AI data centers for a set period, allowing time to assess their environmental and societal impacts. It aims to pause development while stakeholders evaluate energy use, emissions, and regulatory standards before proceeding.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act is designed to make the United States a global frontrunner in artificial intelligence by promoting the development and use of open‑source AI technologies. It outlines measures such as funding, partnerships, and open‑access policies to encourage widespread innovation and ensure that AI benefits a broad range of industries and communities.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: This act is designed to help families avoid the high energy costs associated with large AI data centers. It aims to regulate or cap the power usage of these centers so that the electricity bills and overall costs don’t disproportionately impact households.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes to pause the construction of new large-scale AI data centers to reduce environmental impact and manage resource consumption. It aims to give regulators time to assess and develop guidelines for responsible AI infrastructure development.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 34 - 1.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed law designed to lower regulatory hurdles for AI research and deployment, encouraging faster innovation and broader industry adoption. It also stresses the importance of responsible development and oversight to protect users while boosting economic benefits.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 establishes rules to ensure that AI-powered toys sold to kids are safe, secure, and appropriate for their age. It sets mandatory safety standards, privacy protections, and oversight requirements to guard against potential risks from these AI toys.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Youth AI Privacy Act establishes rules for protecting the privacy of minors in AI applications, ensuring that personal data is safeguarded. It requires companies to obtain parental consent, implement strong data security measures, and provide transparency about how youth data is used.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 47 - 0.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act requires companies and organizations in China to regularly produce and submit detailed reports on their AI system performance, capabilities, and usage. This legislation aims to increase transparency, promote responsible AI deployment, and ensure compliance with national data and security regulations.

title: China AI Power Report Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Foreign Relations.
summary: The China AI Power Report Act likely establishes a framework for organizations to report on the development, deployment, and impact of AI technologies within China. It probably includes oversight provisions and regulatory requirements to ensure AI systems align with national safety, security, and policy objectives.

title: READ AI Models Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The READ AI Models Act is a proposed law that aims to make sure artificial‑intelligence systems are developed, documented, and used safely. It requires companies to disclose how their models work, test them for fairness and reliability, and follow guidelines that protect people from potential harm.

title: A bill to provide for the delivery of artificial intelligence functional bills of materials, and for other purposes.
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Armed Services.
summary: This bill requires that detailed plans or specifications for AI components—known as “functional bills of materials”—be made publicly available to promote transparency and accountability in AI development. It also includes additional provisions to support responsible use and oversight of artificial intelligence technologies.

title: Workforce for AI Trust Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Workforce for AI Trust Act aims to build a skilled and diverse workforce to ensure responsible AI development and deployment. It proposes education, training, and collaboration initiatives to support AI expertise across industry, academia, and government.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 establishes rules to cut the environmental footprint of AI, such as requiring energy‑saving standards and carbon accounting for AI systems. It also mandates companies to report their AI‑related environmental impact, encourages greener AI practices, and provides enforcement tools to ensure compliance.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 aims to prevent AI service providers from charging excessively high prices and from manipulating wages for workers in the AI sector. It introduces regulations that enforce fair pricing and labor practices to protect consumers and employees from exploitative tactics.

title: FARM AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Agriculture.
summary: The FARM AI Act of 2026 is a law that sets rules and safety standards for using artificial intelligence in farming. It aims to help farmers benefit from AI technology while protecting their data and ensuring the tools are used responsibly and ethically.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act is a proposed law designed to encourage the use of artificial intelligence within the financial sector, offering incentives and streamlined regulatory pathways for banks, fintechs, and other financial institutions. It also aims to establish basic safety and ethical guidelines to ensure that AI applications promote transparency, fairness, and consumer protection while boosting innovation and competitiveness.

title: Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act
action: Placed on the Union Calendar, Calendar No. 619.
summary: The Unleashing AI Innovation in Financial Services Act aims to accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence technologies across banking, investing, and insurance sectors, encouraging companies to develop new products and improve operational efficiency. At the same time, it sets up regulatory safeguards—such as data privacy standards, risk‑management protocols, and consumer‑protective measures—to ensure that innovation proceeds responsibly and ethically.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Innovation Talent Act aims to build and sustain a skilled workforce in AI and related fields. It proposes education incentives, research funding, and collaboration between industry and academia to spur innovation and keep the nation competitive.

title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act proposes to ban the construction of AI data centers on federally owned property to protect national resources and minimize environmental impact. It aims to prevent large‑scale AI infrastructure from operating on federal lands, preserving those areas for public use and conservation.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 aims to equip students from kindergarten through high school with the skills and knowledge needed to understand, responsibly use, and critically evaluate artificial intelligence technologies. It proposes curriculum standards, teacher training programs, and public funding to support schools in incorporating AI concepts into everyday learning and fostering digital citizenship.

title: K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026
action: Ordered to be Reported (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 18 - 15.
summary: The K–12 AI Literacy and Readiness Act of 2026 sets a national framework for schools to include artificial‑intelligence education in their curricula, helping students understand how AI works and its impacts. It also requires teacher training, provides resources for equitable access, and establishes standards for measuring AI readiness across schools.

title: CREATE AI Act of 2025
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 29 - 0.
summary: The CREATE AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that sets out rules for designing, testing, and using artificial intelligence systems, with a focus on keeping them safe, clear, and responsible. It requires companies to assess risks, certify their AI products, and keep regulators in the loop so the public’s privacy, fairness, and security are protected.

title: Understanding AI in the Classroom Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Understanding AI in the Classroom Act is a law that aims to help teachers and students learn how to use artificial intelligence responsibly in schools. It sets guidelines for teaching about AI, protects privacy, and encourages digital literacy while making sure AI tools are used safely and fairly.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that every American and community impacted by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center should have the right to transparency and local autonomy.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on the Judiciary, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: This policy states that every citizen and community affected by the construction or operation of an artificial intelligence data center is entitled to clear, open information about those activities and to have a say in how those facilities impact them. It emphasizes that local governments should possess the authority to make decisions that reflect their own interests and safeguard residents’ concerns regarding AI infrastructure.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 aims to ensure that AI technologies used by the VA and other veteran services are safe, ethical, and protect veterans’ privacy. It establishes guidelines, oversight, and accountability standards to promote responsible AI development and deployment for veteran care and benefits.

title: Safeguarding Against Fabricated Exploitation Through Artificial Intelligence Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The AI Act of 2026 is designed to stop people from being harmed by false or deceptive content created by artificial intelligence. It establishes rules and safeguards that developers and users must follow to prevent exploitation through fabricated AI outputs.

title: Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.
summary: The Research and Oversight of AI in Courts Act of 2026 creates a formal structure for studying and monitoring the use of AI tools within the judicial system. It mandates that courts assess how AI affects fairness, transparency, and due process, and establishes an oversight body that reports on compliance and advises on future policy changes.
